subtitle: Zener and bandgap references, scaling to 4.00 V, ratiometric measurement
takeaways: A reference error is a gain error of the chain
Never load a reference: buffer and scale it

slides.title: Regulator or reference?

left.head: Voltage regulator
bullets: Supplies power: mA … A
Accuracy 1–5 %, 100–300 ppm/K
Noise high, rarely specified

right.head: Voltage reference
bullets: Defines a voltage: µA … 10 mA
Accuracy 0.02–1 %, 1–50 ppm/K
Low, specified noise

slides.notes: The ADC measures a ratio, code = 2^N·V_in/V_ref, and the bridge output is a fraction of its excitation: any error of V_ref is a gain error of the whole chain. A reference is a voltage standard on the board; if a load needs current, buffer it with an op-amp.

slides.title: Data sheet parameters
bullets: Initial accuracy at 25 °C (e.g. ±0.1 %) and TC (e.g. 20 ppm/K)
Line and load regulation (e.g. 50 µV/V, 100 ppm/mA)
Noise 0.1–10 Hz peak-to-peak, long-term drift, thermal hysteresis
slides.rule: Box method: TC = (V_{max} − V_{min})/(V_{nom}·(T_{max} − T_{min}))·10^{6} ppm
slides.notes: The box method only uses the extremes, not the shape of the curve: a bandgap's bow looks better or worse depending on the temperature range. Calibration removes the initial accuracy, but not drift and hysteresis.

slides.title: The Zener reference
bullets: Smallest |TC| near 5–6 V: use 5.6 V or 6.2 V Zeners
6.2 V Zener + forward diode: compensated reference diode (1N821)
Fed by a resistor: line regulation ≈ r_{Z}/(R_{V} + r_{Z}), r_{Z} = 5–50 Ω
Fed by a current source: ≈ r_{Z}/r_{o}, far better
slides.notes: Below 5 V the Zener effect has a negative TC, above it the avalanche effect a positive one. The feed choice decides how much supply variation reaches the reference; both feeds are compared in Falstad on the next slide.

slides.title: Falstad: resistor vs current-source feed

falstad.name: zener_resistor
falstad.hint: Supply 12 → 14 V: +7 mV; add 2.2 kΩ load: −17 mV

falstad.name: zener_current_source
falstad.hint: Move the slider to 14 V: VzI changes by only 0.1 mV

observe: Series resistor 1.2 kΩ: 3.5 mV/V line regulation
Current source with r_{o} = 100 kΩ: 70 times better
The load current is taken from the Zener: keep I_{Z} ≥ I_{Z,min}
slides.notes: Read the labels Vz12, Vz14, Vz12L and VzR/VzI. Calculations with the exponential Zener model are in Exercise 4.1 and Exercise 4.2.

slides.title: The bandgap principle
bullets: V_{BE} falls by about 2 mV/K (CTAT)
ΔV_{BE} of two current densities rises with T (PTAT): V_{T}·ln N
Sum V_{BE} + K·ΔV_{BE} ≈ 1.25 V is flat at room temperature
Rule of thumb: about 60 mV per decade of current ratio

falstad.name: delta_vbe
falstad.hint: 1× vs 8× area at the same current: ΔV_BE ≈ 53.8 mV

slides.notes: k/q = 86.2 µV/K; with N = 8, ΔV_BE = 53.5 mV at 25 °C and +0.179 mV/K. I_S cancels, so ΔV_BE depends only on T and N. Falstad has no temperature, but the room-temperature ΔV_BE can be measured.

slides.title: Falstad: Brokaw bandgap cell

falstad.name: brokaw_cell
falstad.hint: Check equal collectors (4.47 V) and 53.8 mV across R2

observe: Op-amp forces equal collector currents; ΔV_{BE} appears across R_{2}
slides.notes: K = 2R_1/R_2 = 11.2 makes the PTAT part rise by +2.0 mV/K, cancelling V_BE. Falstad gives 1.122 V instead of 1.25 V because of its transistor model. Exercise 4.3.

slides.title: Adjustable shunt reference TL431
bullets: Error amplifier compares REF with an internal 2.5 V bandgap
Shunt conducts until V_{REF} = 2.495 V; cathode current 1–100 mA
I_{REF}·R_{1} adds about 24 mV: use smaller resistors or trim

falstad.name: shunt_ref
falstad.hint: Supply 6 V or 12 V: cathode stays at 4.00 V, REF at 2.50 V

slides.notes: Show the behavioural model inside the TL431 (op-amp, 2.5 V source, transistor). R_V must deliver I_K,min plus load and divider current at the lowest supply. Exercise 4.4.

slides.title: Shunt or series reference?

left.head: Shunt (TL431, LM4040)
bullets: Two terminals, any supply above V_{out}
Can serve as negative reference
R_{V} wastes I_{min} + I_{L,max} all the time

right.head: Series (REF50xx, ADR4xx)
bullets: Three terminals, 0.1–1 mA quiescent
Better for varying loads and batteries
Needs V_{in} > V_{out} + V_{dropout}

slides.notes: Both types need decoupling exactly as in the data sheet: some are unstable with the wrong capacitor.

slides.title: Falstad: a divider is no reference

falstad.name: ref_divider_loaded
falstad.hint: 10k/40k at 5 V: 4.00 V open, 2.00 V with the 8 kΩ ladder

falstad.name: ref_buffer_ladder
falstad.hint: 2.5 V × 1.6 = 4.00 V at the ladder top, taps every 0.5 V

observe: Divider source resistance 8 kΩ equals the ladder: voltage halves
A follower restores 4.00 V: input current ≈ 0, output resistance ≈ 0
Non-inverting amplifier scales and buffers in one step
slides.notes: This is the capstone reference for the 3-bit flash converter: 4.00 V on 8 × 1 kΩ, 0.5 mA ladder current. Exercise 4.5.

slides.title: Design recipe: reference for an ADC ladder
steps: Full scale and LSB: LSB = V_{FS}/2^{N} (4.00 V, 3 bit: 0.5 V)
Ladder current I = V_{FS}/(2^{N}·R) (8 × 1 kΩ: 0.5 mA)
Gain G = V_{FS}/V_{R} from a standard reference (2.5 V: G = 1.6)
R_{F}/R_{G} = G − 1, R_{F} + R_{G} ≫ ladder (12 kΩ + 20 kΩ)
Check op-amp current, resistor tolerance, G·V_{offset}; decouple the top
slides.notes: Resistor tolerance enters with (G−1)/G: 1 % resistors give ±0.75 %, about ±30 mV, irrelevant for 3 bit but 30 LSB at 12 bit. Decouple the ladder top with 100–1000 nF close to the comparators.

slides.title: Ratiometric measurement
bullets: Feed sensor divider and ADC ladder from the same V_{ref}
The code then depends only on resistor ratios, not on V_{ref}
Sensor from a fixed 4.00 V, ladder from V_{ref}: 10 % error flips a code
Works only with the same voltage at the same time on both paths

falstad.name: ratiometric
falstad.hint: VREF slider 4.0 → 3.6 V: left stays code 2, right jumps to 3

slides.notes: Two 2-bit flash converters with a 1 kΩ/2.7 kΩ sensor divider, V_in = 0.730·V_exc. A shared connection with voltage drops, or noise on one path only, breaks the cancellation. Exercise 4.6.

slides.title: Error budget of the 4.00 V reference
bullets: Initial 0.20 %, TC 25 ppm/K over ±25 K 0.06 %, resistors 0.08 %
Op-amp offset 0.04 %, long-term drift 0.01 %
Worst case 0.39 %, RSS 0.23 %
3 bit (LSB 12.5 %): no problem; 12 bit: 16 LSB → calibrate
slides.rule: Worst case = sum of all errors, RSS = √(sum of squares)
slides.notes: Compare the budget with the LSB of the converter. After calibration only drift remains: 25 ppm/K over 25 K is still 2.6 LSB at 12 bit (Exercise 4.6). Alternatively measure ratiometrically.
